caption: What if you fell into a black hole? The nearest known one, Gaia BH1, is about 1,560 light-years away. Up close you'd see a black shadow ringed by glowing gas; astronomers took the first photo of one in 2019. Fall into a small black hole and its gravity would stretch you like a noodle. Scientists really call it spaghettification. Pick a giant one, like Sagittarius A* at our galaxy's centre (about 4 million Suns), and you'd cross the event horizon in one piece. A friend watching from far away would see you slow down, freeze and fade. Once inside, escaping would need more than light speed. Indian connection: India-born Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar showed why big stars can end as black holes, and NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory is named after him. Twist: squeeze Earth into a black hole and it would be only about 2 cm wide. Small or giant: which would YOU pick? 👇
